title: Countable amounts: plural partitive
summary: Use plural partitive after paljon or vähän for an unspecified number of separate items: paljon autoja — many cars.
objectives: Use plural partitive after paljon or vähän for an unspecified number of countable things.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use plural partitive after paljon or vähän for an unspecified number of countable things.
Countable things can be separated into individual items. Paljon and vähän leave their number unspecified. The complete plural noun forms are provided.
This lesson practises choosing the plural amount construction; it does not teach every plural stem.
keyPoints: With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.

steps: With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.
Paljon means “a lot of” and works as the quantity word. paljon is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
autoja means “cars” and works as the plural partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep auto and add -ja: auto + ja = autoja.
With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.
Vähän means “a little / few” and works as the quantity word. vähän is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
leluja means “toys” and works as the plural partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep lelu and add -ja: lelu + ja = leluja.
With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.
Paljon means “a lot of” and works as the quantity word. paljon is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.
With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.
Vähän means “a little / few” and works as the quantity word. vähän is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
kuppeja means “cups” and works as the plural partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Change final i to e and keep strong pp: kuppe- + -ja = kuppeja.

commonMistakes: The size of a collection does not turn the noun into a substance noun.
Keep the partitive plural distinct from a nominative -t plural.

practiceExercises.explanation: With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance. Replace final ä with plural i, then add -ä: kyn-i-ä = kyniä.

optionFeedback.kyniä: With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance. Replace final ä with plural i, then add -ä: kyn-i-ä = kyniä.
optionFeedback.kynät: kynät is not the required partitive form for this meaning. With paljon or vähän, several countable things take plural partitive. Here vähän means few, not a little substance.
optionFeedback.kynää: kynää does not express the requested case and number here. Replace final ä with plural i, then add -ä: kyn-i-ä = kyniä.
